style_method: Census: ten women's clothing category pages (tees, tops-shirts, sweaters, jeans, pants, jackets-coats, dresses, skirts, sweatshirts-sweatpants, matching-sets) paged by offset, product URLs de-duplicated on the style code (colourway tiles collapse), giving 231 style codes. Composition read from the product page HTML (the fibre line in the product details list), same origin, one page at a time. Lead fibre = highest share in the first composition listed; lyocell its own fibre; spandex = elastane in the main fabric only (elastomultiester not counted).
sample_basis: 79 of 231 style codes, stratified across the ten category pages in proportion to size (even spacing within each category). Totals are what the category pages yielded on 22 Oct 2026; the pages state no count I could reconcile to, so the 231 may undercount. All 79 sampled pages stated a composition.
fab_basis: Of 79: cotton leads 56 (70.9%); wool 12 (15.2%, six are the SoftWool merino cardigans and sweaters); cashmere 2 (2.5%); silk 1 (1.3%); linen 0; synthetic 3 (3.8%, all polyester); viscose 3, alpaca 1, leather 1. Denim read as the denim cloth: 29 of 79 (36.7%), the jeans plus the four Airy Denim and Regenagri denim shirts and jackets, so 4; with a wider census it could cross 40%. Lyocell appears as a blend component in 11 of 79 (13.9%) but leads none.
tech_named_fabrics: TENCEL(TM) Lyocell and LENZING(TM) ECOVERO(TM) viscose (Lenzing, licensed); own-named cloths Airy Denim, Super Stretch Denim, Comfort Stretch, SoftWool (100% merino), Apres Fleece; third-party Cone and Orta denim named on some jeans pages
tech_owned_or_licensed: licensed (TENCEL, ECOVERO from Lenzing; Regenagri is a farm certification, not a cloth); the other names are Madewell's own marketing names for ordinary cotton, wool and polyester cloths
tech_share_of_range: lyocell in 11 of 79 sampled (13.9%); a named stretch denim (Super Stretch or Comfort Stretch) on 9 of 25 sampled jeans; none is a performance fabric
owned_facility: NONE (no own factory found; Madewell's parent filed in its last 10-K on the investors site, fiscal 2017, that it owns no manufacturing facilities; that filing is old and I found no newer one)
named_makers: NONE (product pages say only "Imported" and never name a factory)
named_mills: partial (Cone denim on 1 and Orta denim on 1 of 25 sampled jeans pages; ISKO named in trade press as a bluesign denim partner, not on the pages I read; the quality page says only "the best denim mills")
made_in_stated_share: 0% (79 of 79 sampled pages say "Imported."; the quality page says over 90% of denim is made in Fair Trade Certified factories, countries not named)
heritage_claim: dated, not placed: "Introduced in 2006, Madewell is a premium denim brand" (about page); no founding place, workshop or maker named
process_documented: no (the quality hub covers sourcing standards: Regenagri cotton, Good Cashmere Standard, Leather Working Group, Fair Trade; it does not describe how anything is made)
craft_reasoning: Madewell states sourcing standards and a share of Fair Trade Certified denim factories but names no factory, owns none, and every sampled product page says only "Imported". Mills are named on 2 of 25 sampled jeans pages (Cone, Orta). That is a stated standard with little checkable beyond it, so a 2; it would move to 3 if the mills or factories were named across the denim range.
note: Part 1 dials read 22 Oct 2026 from madewell.com. Own label only (Madewell sells some outside shoe brands, which are not clothing and not sampled). Madewell also sells men's: women's category pages only, no unisex pieces found in the sample. Sleepwear and swim not sampled. One NYPL collaboration tee is in the sample and counted. status partial only because the census total is unreconciled.

style_method: Category pages for 11 women's clothing categories (T-Shirts, Tank Tops, Hoodies & Sweatshirts, Sweaters & Cardigans, Jackets & Vests, Blouses & Button-Up Shirts, Jeans, Pants & Sweatpants, Skirts, Shorts, Dresses & Jumpsuits). Each page serves only about 30 tiles, so tiles were read in three views per category (default, sale price ascending, sale price descending), giving 520 distinct style codes (style_colour collapsed to style). Composition read from the material field in the product page HTML, one page at a time. Lead fibre = highest share in the first composition listed; recycled polyester counted as polyester, recycled and organic cotton as cotton, TENCEL as lyocell, rayon as viscose, spandex as elastane.
sample_basis: 79 of 520 style codes reachable, stratified in proportion to the category counts the site states (sum 1,246 on 23 Oct 2026; categories overlap so this is not de-duplicated). The 520 are a biased window (featured plus cheapest and dearest tiles), so shares are indicative. One pyjama-set pant was dropped as sleepwear. All 79 sampled pages stated a composition.
fab_basis: Of 79: cotton leads 46 (58.2%); polyester 22 and polyamide 2, so synthetic leads 25 (31.6%); wool 1 (1.3%); linen 1 (1.3%); cashmere 0; silk 0; modal 2, viscose 2, lyocell 2 (cellulosic 7.6%). Denim read as denim cloth: 13 of 79 (16.5%), 12 jeans plus a denim shirt. Graphic tees and sweatshirts are cotton-heavy; knitwear, tanks, dresses and outerwear lean on recycled polyester.
tech_named_fabrics: Next Level Stretch (jeans), Dreamy Drape (denim), Rigid (denim label), Real Good (AE badge for its more sustainable items); lyocell or TENCEL(TM) fibres (Lenzing, licensed) in 9 of 79 sampled (3 labelled TENCEL); Soft & Sexy, Whoa So Soft, Hey Baby are fabric-feel names on knits
tech_owned_or_licensed: own marketing names for denim stretch and drape constructions (Next Level Stretch, Dreamy Drape); TENCEL is licensed from Lenzing; no owned patent or mill found
tech_share_of_range: Next Level Stretch or Dreamy Drape badges on 9 of the 33 jeans tiles read on the jeans page (5 Next Level Stretch, 4 Dreamy Drape) (jeans are 185 of 1,246 category items); lyocell or TENCEL in 9 of 79 sampled styles; not counted across the whole range
owned_facility: NONE (10-K for the year ended 31 Jan 2026: AEO designs and third-party factories manufacture; no owned factories; owns distribution centres)
named_makers: NONE (product pages say only "Imported"; the 10-K names no factories)
named_mills: NONE on product pages (Lenzing named as TENCEL fibre supplier only; no denim or fabric mill named on the 79 pages)
made_in_stated_share: 0% (79 of 79 sampled pages say "Imported"; no country stated)
heritage_claim: dated and placed for the company: first AE store opened 1977 in Twelve Oaks Mall, Novi, Michigan (AEO timeline); nothing on where garments are made
process_documented: no (ae.com and the 10-K describe fits, stretch and sustainability badges, not how garments are made)
craft_reasoning: AEO states in its 10-K that it owns no factories and third parties make everything. All 79 sampled product pages say only "Imported", with no country, factory or mill. The only dated, placed claim is the 1977 first store in Novi, Michigan, which is retail history, not making. Nothing checkable about who makes the clothes, so a 1.
note: Part 1 dials read 22-23 Oct 2026 from ae.com US. Own label only: AE and AE77 Premium (AE77 is AE's own upper line, 14 of 79 sampled). Aerie is a separate brand and not read. AE also sells men's: women's category pages only; unisex pieces not seen in the sample. Sleepwear excluded (one pyjama-set pant dropped), swim not sampled. Status partial: the 520-style window is biased toward featured and price extremes and the site total is not de-duplicated. Shoes sold include outside brands (Ariat, Dr. Martens, Timberland), not clothing and not sampled.

style_method: Ten women's category pages (T-Shirts, Shirts & Blouses, Sweaters & Cardigans, Jeans, Pants, Dresses, Jackets & Coats, Shorts, Skirts, Sweatshirts) paged with the page parameter until a page added no own-label style. Own label = product address starting BDG, UO, Out From Under, Kimchi Blue, Silence + Noise or Urban Renewal, which gave 688 distinct styles; outside brands excluded. Composition read from the Content + Care block in each product page, one page at a time. Lead fibre = highest share in the first composition listed (lining ignored); recycled polyester counted as polyester, rayon as viscose, spandex as elastane.
sample_basis: 78 of 688 own-label styles, stratified in proportion to category size (even spacing within each category). The site states about 4,557 items across the ten categories, outside brands included, so 688 is a floor: pages stopped early and own-label detection is by name. An advent calendar and a pyjama set were dropped. All 78 sampled pages stated a composition.
fab_basis: Of 78: cotton leads 44 (56.4%); synthetic leads 28 (35.9%: polyester 24, acrylic 2, nylon 2); viscose/rayon 5 (6.4%); linen 1 (1.3%); wool 0 as a lead (wool appears as a minor fibre in 2); cashmere 0; silk 0. Denim read as denim cloth: 7 of 78 (9.0%), 6 jeans plus a denim short. Cotton carries BDG, tees, pants, skirts; polyester carries dresses (11 of 16) and sweaters.
tech_named_fabrics: NONE (no named technical or branded fabric in the 78 sampled pages; no TENCEL, Lycra or similar named)
owned_facility: NONE found (the 10-K extract does not mention owned factories; it says UO uses agents and third-party manufacturers and about 4,000 vendors)
made_in_stated_share: 1 of 78 (1.3%): one dress says Made in the USA; the other 77 say "Imported"
heritage_claim: dated and placed: first store opened 1970 across from the University of Pennsylvania, West Philadelphia, by Dick Hayne, Scott Belair and Judy Wicks (URBN history page); nothing on where clothes are made
process_documented: no (the product pages and URBN brand page cover style and community, not making)
craft_reasoning: UO designs and buys from about 4,000 third-party vendors; no owned factory, mill or maker is named on any of the 78 sampled pages, 77 of which say only "Imported". One page says Made in the USA. The only dated, placed claim is the 1970 West Philadelphia first store, which is retail history. Nothing checkable about making, so a 1.
note: Part 1 dials read 22-23 Oct 2026 from urbanoutfitters.com US. Own label only: BDG, UO, Out From Under, Kimchi Blue (sample covers these four). UO sells many outside brands in every category; they are excluded and the site category totals include them. UO also sells men's: women's category pages only. Unisex pieces not identified. Sleepwear and swim excluded (one pyjama set and an advent calendar dropped). Two-piece sets (4 in sample) counted as one style. owned_facility: YES: the Craftsmanship page says production largely takes place in Florence, Italy, "where the brand owns two factories"; the Capri 10-K says Capri owns two luxury footwear manufacturing facilities in Italy that support its brands and Jimmy Choo has a product development facility in Florence
named_makers: NONE (the factories are named by city only; no maker or workshop name on product pages)
named_mills: NONE on product pages; one pump page says it was made using leather certified by a body I did not open
made_in_stated_share: 100% of 26 sampled women's shoe and bag pages state a country: 25 Made in Italy, 1 Made in Vietnam (a shoe); 10-K says most are made in Italy, with other European factories and a small portion in Asia
heritage_claim: dated and placed: bespoke shoes by Jimmy Choo in an East London studio from the 1980s; J. Choo Limited co-founded in 1996 by Jimmy Choo and Tamara Yeardye (now Mellon); first boutique on Motcomb Street, London
process_documented: partial: a Craftsmanship page and "Stories from the atelier" describe designed in London, made in Florence, and hand work with modern methods, with no step-by-step process
craft_reasoning: Jimmy Choo says on its own site that it owns two factories in Florence, and 25 of 26 sampled product pages state Made in Italy, so the maker and the brand are close. It scores 4 not 5 because the owned factories do not cover the whole range (one sampled shoe is made in Vietnam, the 10-K lists other European and Asian makers), no factory or mill is named, and the 10-K is the only filing that says Capri, not Jimmy Choo, owns the factories.
note: Jimmy Choo sells no clothing: tee to outerwear listing links are NONE, fabric dials NONE, and tech left NC (not read; no clothing range to read). Made-in sample: 26 pages across women's shoes (6 each from the main shoes, sandals and boots pages) and bags (8). Read 23 Oct 2026. The "owns two factories" line is the brand's own claim; the 10-K wording differs slightly (Capri owns two footwear facilities in Italy). The Part 0 store counts and the 10-K's 211 stores (incl. concessions, worldwide) are different scopes.
